articles.title: The 2026 65" LG Evo C6 4K OLED TV Drops to $1,199.99 During the eBay Labor Day Sale
articles.summary: LG sells the most OLED TVs, which shouldn't come as a surprise to anyone. Usually the current year model is quite expensive and I typically recommend getting the prior year model for significant cost savings.
body: More sizes are also on sale. C6H models (77", 83") have a Tandem OLED panel.

The C6 is LG's current 2026 model in the LG's C-series OLED TV lineup. The C6 improves upon last year's C5 model with upgraded 165Hz max refresh rate (vs 144Hz) and a new Alpha 11 Gen 3 processor with better AI processing.

LG's C-series OLED TV in general has been our favorite TVs for console gaming for many years thanks to its outstanding image quality, low input lag, and high refresh rate. This is one of the best TVs you can get for streaming 4K HDR content in its intended glory. It boasts the near-infinite black levels, near-infinite contrast ratio, and near-instantaneous response times you'd expect from any OLED TV. It's also equipped with LG's proprietary Evo panel, which is significantly brighter and offers a wider color gamut than traditional W-OLED TVs.

The C6 is also equipped with modern gaming features that make it a perfect complement to current generation consoles like the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X, including a native 120Hz panel that can be pushed to as high as 165Hz, HDMI 2.1 inputs, variable refresh rate and auto low latency mode.

articles.title: Resident Evil's Zach Cregger Admits He Was 'Naive' to Assume Fans Would Approve of Him Avoiding a Direct Adaptation of the Games
articles.summary: Zach Cregger admitted that he was “naive” to think his less-direct approach to adapting Resident Evil would be universally well-received by fans after deliberately choosing to avoid retelling the story exactly as it unfolds in the games.
body: Cregger’s Resident Evil movie follows Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier who gets caught up in the madness of the Raccoon City Incident. The writer/director confirmed previously that this film takes place in parallel to the events of Resident Evil 2 and that it focuses more on what it feels like as a player to navigate through zombie-filled corridors and sneak around Lickers… but not everyone was anticipating an original story told within the continuity of Capcom’s beloved horror game franchise.

Instead, a slew of fans have lashed out at Cregger for not directly adapting an existing game in the series, with many arguing that, without characters like Leon, Ada, and Jill, this isn’t really a Resident Evil movie at all.
IGN’s Tom Jorgensen got the chance to sit down with Cregger to ask him about his feelings on this particular topic — and his response was strikingly self-aware.

articles.title: CD Projekt Red Is Still Raking In The Cash As We Wait For The Witcher 4
articles.summary: CD Projekt Red has released its latest earnings report for the first half of 2026, and in short, it was a banger of a period for the company, and things are only expected to improve with many big-name releases on the horizon.
body: For the January-July period, CD Projekt Red generated 435 million PLN ($116.4 million USD) in revenue, which was up 23% year-over-year. Additionally, the company posted a net profit of 249 million PLN ($66.6 million USD), which was up 37% year-over-year. Total net profitability for the company was a very impressive 57%.

Management said in its report that these strong results were driven in part by "strong sales" of The Witcher and Cyberpunk games. Additionally, CD Projekt said it benefitted nicely from licensing revenue, a category that is becoming more and more important to the company.

The company specifically called out licensing deals that Cyberpunk 2077 had with games like Wuthering Waves and Apex Legends this year. Additionally, the company pointed out how well Cyberpunk TCG did on Kickstarter.

It would appear that CD Projekt's revenues are only set to grow further in the time ahead. That's because the studio has a lot of big games and content on tap, including The Witcher 3 Remastered this year, The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion in 2027, and then The Witcher 4 in 2028.

articles.title: Alienware Just Released the World's First 39" 5K Monitor With RGB Stripe Tandem OLED Technology
articles.summary: Earlier this year, Dell announced the "world's first 39" 5K monitor with RGB stripe tandem OLED technology." You can finally get your hands on one. The new Alienware AW3926QW has just been listed at Dell for $1,099.99 with free delivery (10% less if you have a verified student account).
body: The Alienware AW3926QW has no lack of features that make it stand out from the crowd, but perhaps its most impressive technology is the RGB stripe tandem OLED panel. Tandem OLED stacks multiple OLED layers on top of each other instead of a single layer. Tandem OLED is better than other OLED panels because: 1) it's much brighter (the AW3926QW in particular has a very impressive 1,300 nits of peak brightness) and 2) it's less prone to burn-in.

The AW3926QW doubles down on this with new RGB stripe technology. Whereas traditional tandem OLEDs use white pixels, RGB stripe tandem OLED breaks the color down further into vertically aligned red, green, and blue pixels. This reduces color fringing and in turn significantly improves text clarity. It goes without saying that there are obvious benefits here for both gaming and productivity purposes alike.
points: Earlier this year, Dell announced the "world's first 39" 5K monitor with RGB stripe tandem OLED technology.

articles.summary: The Witcher and Cyberpunk developer CD Projekt Red is staffing up for its unannounced 'Project Hadar', as that team is currently over 30 people strong with plans "to hire more, up to 50 developers by the end of this year," CD Projekt Red vice president of investor relations Karolina Gnas said on…

CDPR also confirmed that the remake of The Witcher 1 is on hold in favor of putting more resources into The Witcher 4, which the studio is targeting for a 2028 release, as well as the just-announced decade-later Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past.

But what is Project Hadar? It's tough to guess at this point, as The Witcher is a third-person fantasy RPG, while Cyberpunk is a first-person RPG shooter. Hadar being an RPG of some caliber is the only reasonably safe bet at this point.

Regardless, CDPR is nothing if not busy, with The Witcher 3 Remastered due out this month (and thankfully, existing owners get upgraded free and, yes, your old save files will work ), plus The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past, The Witcher 4, a Cyberpunk sequel, the aforementioned Witcher 1 remake, and Project Hadar all in development.

articles.title: A Real-Life Romance (And The Love Of Fans) Fueled A Classic NES Remake
articles.summary: With headlines dominated by stories of buyouts, layoffs, employee mistreatment, and crunch, it's easy to think that game development is a constant parade of misery and strife.
body: The Battle of Olympus is a side-scrolling action-RPG released in 1988 by Broderbund for the NES. The visuals and gameplay take a lot of cues from Zelda II, though with a Greek mythology-inspired story and setting and a pretty solid challenge level throughout. It's been described as "a hidden gem" of the NES library many times, often overshadowed by similar titles, but beloved by those who enjoyed it.

Notably, The Battle of Olympus was developed in Japan by a very small developer named Infinity. How small? Well, the game's credits list a whopping three different people--Yukio Horimoto, Reiko Oshida, and Kazuo Sawa. Yukio and Reiko were the two main collaborators, with Yukio handling programming, Reiko on art design, and the pair working together on the game's story. As it turns out, the project would lead the two to discover their connection to each other, and they would marry soon after--making it very fitting that The Battle of Olympus's Japanese subtitle is "The Legend of Love."

articles.title: The 12 Best Star Wars Video Games of All Time, Ranked
articles.summary: On Aug. 27, Electronic Arts released its newest Star Wars game. Star Wars: Zero Company is one of the best reviewed games ever inspired by the series, offering a compelling blend of tactics and fandom that’s nearly impossible to resist.
body: Star Wars video games date all the way back to The Empire Strikes Back on the Atari 2600 in 1982. Since then, the franchise itself has largely matured alongside the medium. Many of the earliest games are still worth revisiting now, even the ones that were victims of hardware limitations. If you’re wondering where to turn first once you complete Zero Company, here are the 12 best Star Wars games of all time.

Respawn Entertainment has had multiple chances to do Star Wars justice, starting with this first entry in the Star Wars Jedi series. It introduces Cal Kestis, a hero living through the dark period following Revenge of the Sith. Not everyone loves the Jedi, even at the best of times. They feel a bit like the galaxy’s superheroes, and yet there’s no denying the thrill of a good lightsaber duel. Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order focuses on that aspect in particular, and lets players explore interesting environments other games only allow them to glimpse from afar. It’s pretty and fun, despite performance issues at launch and some tedious backtracking.

articles.title: Fall 2 Replaces Its Deadly Tower With a Real-Life Nightmare
articles.summary: Sequelizing 2022’s surprise horror-thriller hit Fall could be a simple assignment: Find a bunch of other victims and dangle them from the top of another tower. But like the foolhardy heroes at the center of this week’s Fall 2: Deadpoint, directors Michael and Peter Spierig weren’t looking for a…
body: “We didn't wanna make it a tower or anything similar to the first film,” Peter Spierig tells Polygon. “There was just no point of going there again.”

For the brothers, Fall writer-director Scott Mann set the bar — ahem — high. So, instead of chasing that glory again, they looked at real-world environments that could offer both a visceral thrill more room for character movement and varying set pieces. The solution: recreate China’s Huashan Plank Walk, which by all accounts is… a legit IRL nightmare.

Thousands of people attempt versions of the real-world attraction each year, and videos of it gave the filmmakers a useful preview of exactly what audiences would find terrifying. Their characters could go up and down and left and right.
“We could go sideways and have all kinds of bad things happen,” Peter says.

articles.title: Resident Evil Director Says There’s “No Chance” He’d Survive His Own Movie
articles.summary: Resident Evil games over the years have slowly added more fantastical elements to their tale of bioweapons running amok, but for the new live-action movie, director Zach Cregger is dialing back those ideas to a more "grounded" level.
body: "I feel like some of the Resident Evil games get a little magical," Cregger said during a Reddit Ask Me Anything session (via YouTuber Troy Hill Talks Movies ).

"[Resident Evil] 8, we have a woman who can turn into a bird and fly around. And like, I love it. I've played it a bunch of times. I think it's an awesome game, but in terms of me making a movie out of it, it's like I've got to try and limit some of the wild aspects of Resident Evil. And so I chose to stick with the T-Virus, keep it as grounded as possible. So that means I'm not going to have a gigantic jacked dude in a trench coat, because I'm like, where'd the coat come from? How did he get the coat?"

Cregger explained that while the Resident Evil games do explain how Mr. X gets his stylish coat, in the world he has constructed for the movie, there's no time for the infected bioweapons to consider zombie apocalypse fashion. "This movie, it's like the outbreak just happened," Cregger added. "I want to keep it chaotic, I want to keep it primal, and I want to just keep it as grounded as I can. The T-Virus causes all kinds of cool, fun mutations. That is enough, so I'm limiting it there."

articles.title: 7 Best Games Like Silksong to Play While You Wait for Sea of Sorrows
articles.summary: Just a few months after Hollow Knight: Silksong launched, developer Team Cherry announced a DLC expansion called Sea of Sorrows, set to come out sometime in 2026. With only four months left in the year, fans are starting to get antsy.
body: It’s entirely possible we’re not seeing Sea of Sorrows anytime soon. Longtime fans may remember Silksong itself was originally planned as DLC for Hollow Knight, before growing into a massive, standalone sequel. So, whether you’re waiting a few months or seven years, you could probably use another game or two to pass the time. We’ve rounded up seven games, across genres, that Silksong fans are sure to love.

Zelda 2: The Adventure of Link, alongside Metroid, Faxanandu, and Mega Man, was one of several NES titles that inspired Hollow Knight. Of every game in The Legend of Zelda’s 40-year history, it makes sense that Zelda 2 heavily influenced Team Cherry. For one, it’s unlike any other Zelda game. It’s a side-scroller with RPG elements, reminiscent of some Castlevania titles. It’s also the hardest Zelda game by a long shot. Enemies are fast, lives are limited, and, if you die, you’re sent all the way back to the beginning of the game. Talk about a runback.

articles.title: Kingdom Hearts almost led to Disney making its own version of Super Smash Bros, former dev says
articles.summary: Kingdom Hearts bashing together a bunch of Disney's best toys (and being quite successful in the process) led the Mouse House to briefly begin work on a crossover fighting game in the style of Super Smash Bros.
body: That's according to Ken Christiansen, a former Disney Interactive concept artist who also had credits on the very first Kingdom Hearts game. In an interview with Time Extension, the developer said Kingdom Hearts' world-hopping shenanigans opened Disney's eyes to a whole universe of potential crossover projects.

The development of the original Kingdom Hearts game was apparently a little difficult "because Disney was so reluctant to have that possibility of crossing over The Lion King into The Little Mermaid world," Christiansen recalled.

Disney supposedly "couldn't get over" seeing its most popular characters run into each other constantly, and the company's hesitance meant there was "just a little bit of butting heads" during production, even if most of the developers "thought it was the greatest idea in the world."

Regardless of how unexcited certain Disney executives were about Square Enix 's still-whacky series, it was a pretty major success. The first Kingdom Hearts became one of the PlayStation 2's best-selling games and, as you can imagine, put dollar signs in the eyes of company higher ups.

articles.title: Iconic Banjo-Kazooie composer is more hopeful about a sequel these days, but knows "like three companies" have already been turned down
articles.summary: Grant Kirkhope - the iconic video game composer behind the Donkey Kong Rap and the Banjo-Kazooie games - thinks a potential Banjo-Threeie is slightly more likely now.
body: Almost three decades have passed since Banjo-Kazooie's last mainline platformer flapped onto the N64 and it's been almost 20 years since Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts and Bolts flopped onto the Xbox 360, but it's never too late for another adventure with the bird and bear.

Speaking to FRVR, Kirkhope explained that he used to feel there was "zero chance of another Banjo-Kazooie game." Nowadays, that sentiment's been upgraded to a "slight chance" because he thinks Rare's updated leadership could be more receptive to an outside developer spearheading a threequel.

"Rare just typically say no to everything," the composer explained. "I've known people present cartoons to them, all sorts of ideas, and they just say no to everything." But since former studio head Craig Duncan stepped down from his role at Xbox Game Studios, Kirkhope reckons Rare might be "a little bit different right now" and "a bit more open to discussion."

articles.title: CD Projekt mystery games update: Yes, they're still happening, and no, not any time soon
articles.summary: CD Projekt has a lot going on these days: The Witcher 4, Cyberpunk 2, a new Witcher 3 expansion and remaster, a remake of the original Witcher, probably some other stuff I've either forgotten or don't know about, and a couple of long-simmering mystery projects that are still only known by their…
body: You'd be forgiven for forgetting about them, given their low profile and drawn-out development times, but in today's H1 investors call, CD Projekt's vice president of investor relations Karolina Gnaś reassured everyone that they're still happening—just not anytime soon.
Asked about Sirius, Gnaś mentioned the recent cuts to the development team, saying—as CD Projekt did when the layoffs happened—that the changes were made to meet "the current needs of the project."

"Pre-production is ongoing, and at this stage we are focused on testing different solutions and ideas we develop," Gnaś said. "This project is very different from our other projects because it's focused on multiplayer. So there's a lot of learning and testing in this particular one."

Sirius first came to light in 2021, when CD Projekt acquired The Molasses Flood, known for The Flame in the Flood, to work on a new game eventually revealed to be based on The Witcher. But the project ran into trouble a couple years later, and was paused and rebooted; in 2025, CD Projekt's plan to maintain The Molasses Flood as an effectively independent studio also came to an end.

With the support of Winston Churchill (Michael Sheen), Ian Fleming (Art Malik) and an extraordinary network of double agents, among them Dusko Popov (Nicolas Cage), the real-life spy who inspired the James Bond novels, Juan Pujol (Jordi Mollà), a Spanish chicken farmer, and Nancy Armstrong (Alice Eve), a top British Intelligence agent, they create a spectacular master plan using a fictitious army, fake tanks, aircraft and ships, actors and false radio messages to fool Hitler’s Nazi Army in the build-up to D-Day. videos.summary: An extended look into Crombie’s experiment.
body: In ONTOS, you play as Aditi as she explores the repurposed moon hotel Samsara and encounters strange Experiments and other disturbing scenarios. Your morality will be tested.
In this video, we’ll take you deeper into one such experiment led by Crombie, a scientist drawn to Samsara in search of answers about the essence of one’s unique, individual self.
Do you trust the machine? Do you seek an alternative approach?
